gml:Dictionary.gml:description: Controlled vocabulary for diggs:AbstractSamplingActivityType/samplingCategory (realized by diggs:SamplingActivity) - ISO 22475-1:2021's sampler/technique capability categories, describing how much a sampling technique disturbs the material being sampled, independent of what was actually recovered (see diggs:SampleType/qualityClass for the sample-side counterpart, soil only). Categories A-E apply identically in structure to both soil (ISO 22475-1 section 5.3) and rock (section 5.4), each with its own definition; Category A is least disturbance, and the second (2021) edition of the standard added Categories D and E beyond the first edition's A-C. PROVISIONAL: verified against the standard's own foreword and table of contents (primary source), but the specific defining criteria for each category, especially the 2021-new D and E, are drawn from a secondary source (a named, dated trade-journal article directly quoting the prior edition's EC7-2 Table 1) rather than the paywalled standard text itself - see docs/build/R16/NOTES.md section 10 in the rigid-inclusions repo. Confirm against the full standard before treating the category-level descriptions as final.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Sampling Category

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Least disturbance to the material's fabric and structure; the only category able to yield samples suitable for strength and compressibility/stiffness testing (soil quality class 1) or equivalent high-quality rock samples.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Category A sampling

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Structure and composition largely preserved but with more disturbance than Category A; unsuitable for strength or compressibility testing, still reliable for density- and permeability-related classification.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Category B sampling

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Material and stratigraphic sequence identifiable but particle size, water content and finer structure are no longer reliably representative of in-situ conditions; in the 2006 first edition this was the most disturbed of three categories.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Category C sampling

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Introduced in the 2021 second edition as a further disturbance gradation between the original Category C and the new Category E. PROVISIONAL - defining criteria not sourced beyond the standard's table of contents; see the dictionary description.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Category D sampling

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Introduced in the 2021 second edition as the most disturbed category, extending beyond the original three-category (A-C) scheme. PROVISIONAL - defining criteria not sourced beyond the standard's table of contents; see the dictionary description.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Category E sampling
